title: Finding the top-k elements with a min heap
summary: Maintain at most k candidates in a min heap and compare its minimum against each remaining element to retain the largest k values step by step.
context: In this example, k = 3; the input array and its indices are listed in the table below. Pointer i denotes the input index, while heap is the level-order array of the min heap: heap index 0 holds the smallest candidate, with left and right children at heap indices 1 and 2 (when present). Input indices indicate where each element came from, whereas heap indices indicate its current storage slot.

First insert the initial k input elements into the heap one by one, then compare each remaining element against the heap top: if the current value exceeds the heap top, remove the heap top and insert the current value; otherwise skip it. State tables are named by step number; steps that only compare or skip leave the heap unchanged and refer by caption to the active table of candidates and source indices.
description: The heap top holds the smallest value among the current candidates. Whenever a larger value arrives, replacing the heap top with it preserves the largest k values seen so far. Checking the heap top takes O(1) time, and each insertion or removal takes O(log k) time.
result: Because the heap retains at most k candidates, space complexity is O(k) and total time complexity is O(n log k).

frames.title: Insert 1 into the empty heap
frames.explanation: At pointer i = 0, read value 1 and insert it into the empty heap. There is now 1 candidate, [1], and the heap top is 1.
frames.key_state: Value 1 from input index i = 0 is inserted; the heap has 1 item [1], with heap top 1.
frames.announcement: Insert 1 into the empty heap; the heap is now [1].

frames.title: Insert 7 into the heap
frames.explanation: At pointer i = 1, read value 7 and insert it at heap index 1. Parent node 1 is smaller than 7, so no sift-up is needed; the 2 candidates are [1, 7], and the heap top is 1.
frames.key_state: Value 7 from input index i = 1 is inserted; the heap has 2 items [1, 7], with heap top 1.
frames.announcement: Insert 7 into the heap with no sift-up needed; the heap is now [1, 7].

frames.title: Insert 6; initial candidates ready
frames.explanation: At pointer i = 2, read value 6 and insert it at heap index 2. The 3 candidates are now [1, 7, 6], with heap top 1; all first k = 3 inputs are in the heap, so subsequent elements will be compared against the heap top.
frames.key_state: Value 6 from input index i = 2 is inserted; the initial 3 items [1, 7, 6] are in place, with heap top 1.
frames.announcement: Insert 6 into the heap; the initial three candidates [1, 7, 6] are ready, with heap top 1.

state_tables.caption: Step 3 candidates: initial three items ready

frames.title: Compare current value 3 with heap top 1
frames.explanation: At pointer i = 3, current value 3 is greater than the smallest candidate 1, so a replacement will follow. This step only compares without removing or inserting yet; the 3 candidates remain [1, 7, 6], with heap top 1. For candidates and source indices, see table “Step 3 candidates: initial three items ready.”
frames.key_state: At input index i = 3, current value 3 > heap top 1, preparing to replace; the heap is not yet modified and still has 3 items [1, 7, 6], with heap top 1.
frames.announcement: Compare current value 3 with heap top 1: since 3 > 1, prepare to replace; the heap is not yet modified.

frames.title: Remove former heap top 1
frames.explanation: With pointer still at i = 3, first remove former heap top 1, leaving [6, 7] with temporary heap top 6. Only k − 1 = 2 candidates are in the heap while value 3 awaits insertion; this is an intermediate state of the replacement rather than the end of the round, and no result is lost.
frames.key_state: At input index i = 3, former heap top 1 is removed; the heap temporarily holds k − 1 = 2 items [6, 7] with heap top 6 while current value 3 awaits insertion.
frames.announcement: Remove former heap top 1; the heap temporarily holds 2 items [6, 7] while 3 awaits insertion.

state_tables.caption: Step 5 candidates: intermediate state after removing 1

frames.title: Insert 3 into the heap
frames.explanation: With pointer still at i = 3, insert value 3 into the heap and sift it up to the root, restoring k = 3 candidates [3, 7, 6] with new heap top 3. These three candidates are the largest three values among the first 4 inputs.
frames.key_state: At input index i = 3, 3 is inserted and sifted up, restoring 3 items [3, 7, 6] with heap top 3.
frames.announcement: Insert 3 and sift it up as the new heap top, restoring three candidates [3, 7, 6].

frames.title: Compare current value 2 with heap top 3
frames.explanation: At pointer i = 4, current value 2 is smaller than heap top 3 and does not qualify for replacement. This step only compares, leaving the 3 candidates as [3, 7, 6]. For candidates and source indices, see table “Step 6 candidates: after inserting 3.”
frames.key_state: At input index i = 4, current value 2 < heap top 3, so no replacement occurs; the heap keeps 3 items [3, 7, 6] with heap top 3.
frames.announcement: Compare current value 2 with heap top 3: since 2 < 3, do not replace.

frames.title: Skip 2
frames.explanation: At pointer i = 4, because 2 is smaller than heap top 3, skip it without removing or inserting. The 3 candidates remain [3, 7, 6] with heap top 3, and all inputs have now been processed. For candidates and source indices, see table “Step 6 candidates: after inserting 3.”
frames.key_state: Value 2 at input index i = 4 is skipped and all inputs are processed; the heap keeps 3 items [3, 7, 6] with heap top 3.
frames.announcement: Skip 2; the three candidates [3, 7, 6] remain unchanged and all inputs are processed.

frames.title: Return the three candidates
frames.explanation: Traversal is complete with no active pointer, so return the min heap [3, 7, 6] directly. Their source input indices are listed in the table below; the heap top is 3, while left and right children 7 and 6 need not be in ascending order because no final sort is performed.
frames.key_state: Traversal complete, no active pointer; return min heap [3, 7, 6] of 3 items with heap top 3, not sorted in ascending order.
frames.announcement: Return min heap [3, 7, 6]; the returned elements are not sorted in ascending order.

state_tables.caption: Step 9 final returned candidates and sources
